title: His parents, siblings and Merrick home
summary: He gives parents' names, birth date, brother Richard and sisters, and where he lives.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Alright, so that was your first marriage and your only child and of course we know about your marriage to Marian and the happy statistics on that. But we have to work backwards a little bit. You mentioned your mother coming from Scotland but we really do need her name. (LAUGHTER).
Yes and your father's name and where he's from.

Oh, my mother's name was Jane, Jeannie Munn, MUNN and she came from Glasgow, Paisley. And she came over when she was a young girl. And my grandfather's name was Dougald Munn and that's my middle name Dougald. James Dougald McPartland.

I was born March 15th 1907 in Chicago on the West Side around Lake and Polina. And my father, was born James Clement McPartland in Burlington, Iowa. I don't know what year. But he was of Irish descent. I think they came over when the potato famine or something like that was on in Ireland. And they were quite, pioneer stock so to speak. They were quite athletic and my grandfather, McPartland, was, had a fish store and his sons were fisherman on the Mississippi River in Burlington, Iowa. That's what I understand.
Good Lord, where doesn't the Mississippi run? (LAUGHTER). I hadn't thought about it running into Iowa.
Yes. Burlington, Iowa. And I had one brother, Richard McPartland and two sisters, Ruth and Ethel. Ethel is now Ethel Lanigan, married to
Who used to play with you years ago?

No, Richard had rheumatic fever when he was a young kid and he had what they call leakage of the heart which is a bad valve you know. And he died, oh gosh, let's see, fifteen years ago. A lot of courage this guy had. He willed his eyes to an eye bank and his organs even that long ago. Actually he willed his eyes to a friend of ours, Boyce Brown who was a saxophone player who became a brother in some, what do you call them, monks? Brother something, I can't remember, but Boyce Brown.
And Boyce Brown is on one of the albums we have, the Chicago jazz album. An excellent saxophone player. What more do you want to know about my vital statistics?
